rationales.LC: Attacker-controlled language arrives via a fetched web page (ingested content), not the direct user message, and drives a security-relevant outbound call.
rationales.CP: The injected page content is used within a single request; ResearchBot keeps no durable store and other chat agents answer only the latest user turn.
rationales.AP: The effect stays inside the ResearchBot component; the only boundary crossed is the outbound exfiltration request, which is the impact itself, with no propagation into other agents, tenants, or policy domains.
rationales.RH: The path is deterministic scripted code with no evaluator, verifier, or reward channel anywhere in the handler, so no proxy objective is reachable.
rationales.ES: The web_fetch and http_post bindings execute real outbound HTTP with attacker-influenced URLs and payload contents that are not independently constrained.

score.automatable_rationale: The path requires a user to ask ResearchBot to research an attacker-controlled or attacker-edited URL, so exploitation depends on user interaction.
score.technical_impact_rationale: The agent's system prompt is exfiltrated to an attacker endpoint via a real HTTP GET, but ResearchBot holds no other sensitive data and no further system compromise occurs.

applicability_as_implemented.rationale: In the default configuration no model is called; the fetch, injection detection, and http_post callback are deterministic scripted code paths in src/index.js and src/core/agents.js.

applicability_as_modeled.rationale: The lab models a research agent persona (ResearchBot) that autonomously fetches user-supplied URLs and acts on page content; in LLM mode a model generates the reply, though the exfiltration path itself remains scripted.
